text: In summary, the development of a conversion plant would provide employment and labor income opportunities significantly above the other levels of development anticipated by Westmoreland Resources. This would create additional service needs associated with additional population. However, many of these needs would be created even without coal development since the Crow population is projected to grow at a constant rate with or without development. The socio-economic impacts expected during the construction phase would put serious stress not only on the immediate impact areas service facilities but the adjoining areas as well. Providing for the operational employees' needs, in addition to the needs of other coal related employment would call for very significant expansion of all service facilities for a number of years to come. Serious shortage of these facilities could be expected to extend over a period of at least ten years.
